data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in Report 1 (qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507), which failed to review the Makefile due to an API BadRequestError. Report 2 (deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed the same Makefile and confirmed it contains only standard AUR build automation commands (makepkg --printsrcinfo, makepkg -s) with no security issues. This is not a genuine security disagreement but a coverage gap due to tool failure.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507) failed to review Makefile due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), resulting in inconclusive verdict
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should be distinguished from genuine security uncertainty when determining final verdicts
When multiple models review the same package and one fails due to tool error while another succeeds, the successful review should resolve the disagreement rather than defaulting to inconclusive
The audit tool should implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for API failures to prevent coverage gaps
Inconclusive verdicts due to tool errors should be flagged separately from inconclusive verdicts due to ambiguous security findings
